title: ThinK: Explorative Modeling for Fine-Grained Geometry Estimation, from Regression to Flow Matching
teaser: Thin structures come out bent in feed-forward geometry estimation because a pointwise loss must predict the mean of two competing surfaces — a diagnosis the field has converged on, with per-pixel depth mixtures (MDA) and generative flow matching (PointDiT) as the current fixes. This project studies a third: best-of-K exploration (Explorative Modeling) at both ends of the objective spectrum — a one-pass latent-conditioned head whose shared latent commits to a jointly coherent surface assignment rather than per-pixel marginals, and a few-step flow-matching depth model — asking how much generation factoring fine-grained geometry still needs once the objective can commit.
abstract: Feed-forward geometry estimators such as MoGe and Depth Anything 3 recover global structure remarkably well, yet their local geometry fails in a characteristic way: thin structures — streetlamps, chair legs, railings — emerge bent or oscillatory in 3D, with distortion growing as the structure gets thinner and the background more distant (SurGe). The diagnosis is by now established: around a thin structure the per-pixel conditional p(depth | image) is bimodal (foreground or background), and a deterministic regressor trained with a pointwise loss must predict the conditional mean — a point floating between the two surfaces that no real scene contains. Two fixes exist. PointDiT swaps regression for generative flow matching (boundary F1 10.9 to 13.9 on the same architecture), paying with multi-step sampling machinery; MDA replaces the final layer with an explicit per-pixel mixture-density head and selects one depth hypothesis per pixel, so predictions land on a real surface. Both leave a gap: per-pixel mixtures model marginals and select each pixel independently, so nothing couples the chosen surface along a thin structure — yet a thin structure is a correlated string of ambiguous pixels whose right description is the joint mode (this whole strip is the pole), while multi-step sampling buys joint coherence with inference steps. Explorative Modeling (XM) targets exactly this gap: draw K candidate predictions per training step and backpropagate only the best-matching one, which provably turns the loss minimizer from the mean into committed modes (best-of-K squared error is a K-means-style quantization of the conditional) — with a shared latent that commits to a jointly coherent assignment, and applicable to both objectives. Arm A (end-to-end XM on regression): a lightweight latent-conditioned refinement head on a frozen backbone, trained with best-of-K selection under an edge-sensitive scoring loss (point gradient matching), keeping inference a single forward pass; K=1 is the exact regression baseline. Arm B (hybrid XM on flow matching): fine-tune a released pixel-space few-step depth model (Pixel-Perfect Depth) with exploration over its input noise — same data sample and timestep, K noise draws, train the best coupling — leaving the sampler untouched. Hypotheses: (i) in both arms, boundary F1 and point-map normal error improve monotonically with K while AbsRel/delta1 stay flat; (ii) the failure mode transforms from off-manifold averaging (bent poles) to on-manifold commitment (straight, possibly sub-pixel-shifted poles), with a jointly coherent surface assignment along thin structures where per-pixel winner-take-all can oscillate; (iii) exploration substitutes for generation factoring — with enough K, the one-pass regression arm approaches the few-step flow arm, and the flow arm needs fewer sampling steps to reach its best quality — replicating XM's jumps-versus-exploration tradeoff on a perception task; (iv) enumerating the K latents yields multi-hypothesis geometry whose spread is a calibrated, boundary-localized uncertainty. Exploration cost is modest (each candidate adds roughly a forward pass, so XM-K costs about (K+2)/3 standard steps) and is reported under matched training compute.
milestones: Literature review (Explorative Modeling and its best-of-K lineage — IMLE, multiple choice learning, mixture density networks and MDA's per-pixel depth mixtures; the substitution between exploration and generation factoring; local-geometry evaluation and the point-gradient-matching loss from SurGe; the generative-vs-regression controlled comparison in PointDiT); stand up the shared evaluation — boundary F1, point-map normal error, AbsRel/delta1, thin-structure crops on iBims-1, ETH3D, and GSO. Kill test: on a synthetic bimodal-edge toy set (thin foreground rods over distant backgrounds), verify best-of-K training sharpens exactly what K=1 provably blurs, for both a toy regressor and a toy flow model.

Arm A — end-to-end XM on regression: train a lightweight refinement head with a latent input (Gaussian noise channel or K learned embeddings) on a frozen backbone (MoGe or Depth Anything 3) on Hypersim; sweep K in {1, 2, 3, 5, 8} with K=1 as the exact baseline; ablate the selection criterion — global pointwise loss versus edge-weighted point-gradient-matching scoring — since thin structures occupy few pixels and a global argmin dilutes their signal.

Arm B — hybrid XM on flow matching: fine-tune the released Pixel-Perfect Depth checkpoint with best-of-K exploration over input noise (same sample, timestep, and conditioning per candidate; per-sample loss selection; winner re-forwarded with gradients); sweep K at the default sampler, then sweep sampling steps (1/2/4) at fixed K to test whether exploration lets the model keep quality with fewer steps.

The head-to-head: compare both arms, their K=1 baselines, and an MDA-style per-pixel mixture-density head trained on the same frozen backbone — isolating explicit per-pixel mixtures versus implicit joint latents versus flow matching — under matched training compute: boundary and normal metrics at depth discontinuities, spatial coherence of the committed surface assignment along thin structures, global AbsRel/delta1, NFE at inference, and qualitative point clouds (does bent become committed-but-straight?); chart quality versus (K, sampling steps) to map the exploration-versus-factoring frontier for geometry.

(Stretch) Multi-hypothesis geometry and uncertainty: enumerate the K latents at inference for diverse plausible reconstructions of ambiguous regions, evaluating candidate spread as a boundary-localized uncertainty estimate; or per-region best-of-K selection to cover multiple independent thin structures per image.
